NSA Haiku Generator

2013
Web-based generative software, Twitter integration, interactive installation

Made with web designer Britt Boyd after the 2013 Snowden revelations, NSA Haiku Generator writes poetry entirely from a Department of Homeland Security list of about 750 terms flagged by surveillance systems. Each term carries a syllable count, so the generator can assemble random haiku in the traditional 5-7-5 form: “Cocaine Keylogger / Roswell Planet-1 rail gun / nuclear elvis.” Visitors are invited to share their haiku under #NSAHaiku, flooding the internet with the very words the government searches for and, in principle, making the surveillance a little less effective. It was shown as an interactive installation in “Heavily Scripted: Generative Art and Bots,” curated by Lee Tusman at Little Berlin, Philadelphia.
